per_view.notes: Slender grey tube with a boxy raised upper deck over the front third and a dashed main-deck window line plus upper-deck windows. Under the wing only two or three blunt box nacelles are discernible, intersecting each other with no clear pylons. Wing reads as a thin swept sliver, no taper depth. Tall swept fin present; tiny horizontal stab. Nose gear is a single thin stick; main wheels are bare cyli

Slender light-grey tube with a front-mounted rounded upper-deck capsule sitting proud of the crown (visible seam, no fairing). Even main-deck window band plus upper-deck windows; no cockpit windshield. Two blocky box nacelles, one extending aft of the wing, pylons unclear. Wings read as thin flat slivers. Tall swept fin present; thin tailplane. Gear: single nose wheel, three tiny wheels, no bogies

Head-on: four dark-inlet nacelles on pylons under swept wings, correct inboard/outboard spacing. Nose bulges with a raised crown reading as the hump; a thin cockpit windshield band is the only surface detail — no other windows or doors. Tall fin visible; horizontal stabilizers read as thin slivers. Nose gear plus two visible main struts; wing dihedral is minimal and wings look slab-thin.

Rear head-on: four pylon-mounted nacelles under swept wings with plausible inboard/outboard spacing. Wings show mild dihedral and taper. Tail shows only a tall, very thin spike-like fin; no horizontal stabilizers are visible from this angle. Gear: nose strut plus several main bogies. Surfaces are uniformly flat grey; no windows, doors, or livery accents.

Top-down: slender light-grey tube, rounded nose, oval hump fairing in front third. Four grey cylinders sit on the wing leading edges, reading as upright stubs rather than underslung nacelles with open inlets; no forward-offset pylon shape. Wings swept and tapered but span looks short. Dashed side lines suggest windows. Small swept fin and tailplanes present; assembly clean, engine junctions crude.

Fuselage is a plain slender tube with a rounded nose and no upper-deck hump at all, so it reads as a generic four-engine narrow-body, not a 747. Four nacelles hang on pylons under swept, tapered wings. Single window band of dark specks, no cockpit glazing. Only a small nose gear; no main gear. Visible seam ring behind the nose. Uniform grey/white finish.

Nacelles read as short cylinders bunched near the wing root/trailing area rather than four evenly spaced pylon-hung pods offset ahead of the leading edge; they intersect the wing. Partial front hump with upper-deck windows is clear, main-deck window line is even. Wings swept but slab-like; rear fuselage ends in a blunt flat cylinder cut, no upswept tail cone. Gear struts small but present.

Slender grey tube with tapered nose and tail cone; swept fin plus horizontal stabilizers. Upper-deck crown is only a faint step near the nose, not an iconic hump. Four nacelle-like cylinders present but scattered, one hanging low, pylons not visible; wings read as thin edge-on slabs. Nose strut and two main bogies visible. Uniform flat grey, no accent.

Hump is a separate cylinder capped with a hard circular seam sitting on the crown, starting behind the nose rather than faired from the cockpit; no cockpit windshield. Dashed main-deck and upper-deck window rows are even. Swept wings, dark-inlet pylon nacelles, swept fin and tailplane, nose and clustered main gear visible. Coherent grey/white livery; visible fuselage step.

critic.fix_suggestion: Improve 'Landing gear (nose gear + 4-truck main gear) when visible' (mean 5.38/10). Target the 8 anchor: nose gear plus four main-gear trucks under the wing/body junction with wheels; then the 10 anchor: recognizable 747 gear layout: two-wheel nose strut, four multi-wheel main bogies (two under the body, two under the wings), plausible strut lengths.
